draft.title: Perspectives in the past
card: A perspective is a point of view. It is how a person sees an event or an issue.
A person's perspective is shaped by their place in society, such as being rich or poor, a ruler or a worker.
It is also shaped by their beliefs and by the time they lived in. People in the past often held ideas that are different from ours.
Two people can live through the same event and see it differently. A pharaoh and a farmer may not have seen a flood, a war or a new tax in the same way.
draft.remember: People see the same event differently because of who they are, what they believe and when they live.

a.q: Why might a pharaoh and a farmer in ancient Egypt describe the same tax differently?
opts: Their place in society gave them different points of view
One of them must have been lying about the tax
Only the pharaoh lived at the time the tax was set
The farmer could not have had any view about the tax
a.why: A pharaoh and a farmer held different places in society, so each saw the tax from a different point of view. It is wrong to say one must be lying, because a different perspective does not mean a false account.
a.clue: Think about how each person's position in society shapes what they see.

b.q: A wealthy landowner and a labourer both wrote about a harsh drought in ancient Rome. Their accounts differ. What is the best explanation?
opts: Each wrote from a different position in society
The drought happened twice, once for each writer
The labourer's account must be the false one
Only the landowner's account counts as evidence
b.why: The two writers held different places in society, so the drought affected them and looked to them in different ways. The labourer's account is not false just because it differs, since a perspective is a point of view and not an error.
b.clue: Ask how each writer's life and position might change what they noticed.

a.best: Their place in society gave them different points of view

b.best: Each wrote from a different position in society

proposal.title: Perspectives in the past
card: A perspective is a point of view. It is how a person sees an event or an issue.
A person's perspective is shaped by their place in society, such as being a ruler or a worker. A pharaoh and a farmer felt a new tax in very different ways.
It is also shaped by their beliefs and by the time they lived in. People in the past often held ideas that are different from ours.
Two people can live through the same event and describe it differently. A different view is not the same as a mistake, so both accounts can be honest.
proposal.remember: Who you are, what you believe and when you live shape how you see an event.

a.q: In the same year in ancient Egypt, a pharaoh praised a new tax and a farmer complained about it. What best explains this?
opts: Each saw the tax from their own place in society
The farmer got the facts about the tax wrong
The pharaoh and farmer lived at different times
Their accounts describe two different taxes
a.why: A pharaoh and a farmer held very different places in society, so the same tax looked different to each of them. It is tempting to think the farmer got it wrong, but a different view is not the same as a mistake.
a.clue: Both are talking about the same tax in the same year.

b.q: During one drought in ancient Rome, a landowner wrote it caused little trouble. A labourer wrote that families went hungry. Which is the best conclusion?
opts: Both can be honest, seen from different places in society
The landowner got it wrong, since he played down the hunger
The labourer got it wrong, since she overstated the hunger
The accounts describe two separate droughts in Rome
b.why: A rich landowner with grain to spare and a poor labourer would feel the same drought in different ways, so both accounts can be honest. Calling either one wrong is tempting, but differing accounts can show different perspectives rather than mistakes.
b.clue: Could one drought hit a rich family and a poor family equally hard?

a.best: Each saw the tax from their own place in society

b.best: Both can be honest, seen from different places in society
